Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Sacramento CA
1222 PM PST Wed Nov 4 2026

.KEY MESSAGES... 
 
 - Dry weather, above normal temperatures, and periodically breezy
   north to east winds through the weekend and into next week

 - Slight chance for light rain showers in Shasta County Sunday
   into next week

 - Potential shift toward active weather pattern mid to late next
   week

&&

.DISCUSSION...

Today-Saturday:

High pressure over the region is promoting dry weather and
seasonably high temperatures across interior Northern California
today. Despite some high level clouds streaming around the
northern periphery of the ridge, mostly sunny skies are observed.
Afternoon temperatures have been running generally 5 to 15 degrees
warmer compared with yesterday's reading, with highs in the upper
50s to 60s across the Valleys and Foothills, and mid 40s to 50s 
over the mountains. A period of breezy north winds is expected 
through the Valley/Delta this afternoon and Thursday afternoon, 
with the breezier conditions west of Interstate 5 where gusts from
15-25 mph are expected, transitioning to breezy downslope 
easterlies along the Sierra overnight into Thursday. Tonight into 
Thursday, low clouds and patchy fog/mist is expected to 
redeveloped along the eastern side of the Valley. 

The ridge will amplify across the region through the end of the
week. A drying and warming trend is expected through the weekend,
with near to above normal temperatures. Resultant high temperatures
into the 70s are anticipated across the Valley/foothills and 60s 
throughout the mountains. Periods of breezy north winds will 
continue through the Valleys each afternoon, with locally breezy 
northeasterly/downslope winds develop each overnight through mid 
morning period in the mountains and foothills as well, especially 
for the typical wind- prone locations and northeast/east to 
southwest/west aligned drainages. For these areas, strongest winds
gusting 25-35 mph are expected late Friday into Saturday. 


Sunday-Next Week:

As the ridge axis shifts eastward a broad area of west-southwest 
flow aloft looks to build in Sunday into next week alongside 
persistently high heights aloft. This will usher in a gradual 
return toward light onshore flow, although high temperatures do 
look to remain near to above normal into the early week ahead. 
While available moisture early in the week will limit overall 
precipitation potential, any ejecting shortwaves will introduce at
least light shower chances for portions of Shasta County to begin
the week. 

Ensemble guidance still generally indicates potential for a shift
toward an active weather pattern, including chances for heavy 
rain and heavy mountain snow, around the mid to late next week 
period. A high degree of uncertainty still accompanies the 
forecast relative to this potential shift though. The anticipated 
southward progression of deep troughing over the Gulf of Alaska 
toward the California coast remains the largest piece of 
uncertainty at this time. Persistent ridging and high heights 
aloft across much of interior California have so far staved off 
this robust system. Given the deep fetch of available moisture 
offshore and general ensemble trends for the aforementioned trough
to break through and dig southward by mid next week, the WPC 8-14
day outlook (Nov. 10-16) continues to highlight a moderate risk 
for heavy rain and heavy mountain snow, and a slight chance for
high winds. Be sure to stay up to date with the latest forecast 
information and check back for updates as we get closer.

&&

.AVIATION...

Sites have cleared this morning, returning to general VFR 
conditions after 18z. Breezy north winds 8-12 kts are expected to 
continue at TAF sites through 00z Thursday before light winds
return. As winds weaken after 00z Thursday, another period of 
MVFR/IFR conditions in BR/FG will be possible throughout the 
Valley into Thursday morning as well with best chances after 12z
Thursday.

&&

.STO WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
None.
